name: Saskop
description: Saskop (also known as Lambapea) is an Estonian trick-taking card game for four players. It is the Estonian member of the prestigious Schafkopf group of games. It distinguishes itself with a 36-card deck (removing 5s and lower) and a complex ranking system where the 6s and Kings occupy the highest tiers of the trump suit. It is a partnership game that emphasizes card counting and aggressive bidding to secure the 61-point victory threshold.

overview.description: Saskop (also known as Lambapea) is an Estonian trick-taking card game for four players. It is the Estonian member of the prestigious Schafkopf group of games. It distinguishes itself with a 36-card deck (removing 5s and lower) and a complex ranking system where the 6s and Kings occupy the highest tiers of the trump suit. It is a partnership game that emphasizes card counting and aggressive bidding to secure the 61-point victory threshold.

history.origins: Derived from the German Schafkopf games brought to the Baltics in the 19th century. It evolved into a distinct Estonian folk game, adopting the name 'Lambapea' (Sheep's Head) in parallel with its German ancestor.
timeline: 1880s: Schafkopf variants are documented in Estonian university circles.
1930s: Saskop emerges as a staple in rural Estonian social life.
1990s: Post-independence resurgence as a traditional cultural pastime.
Present: Played competitively in Estonian card clubs and online forums.
history.cultural: In Estonia, Saskop is often associated with long social gatherings and communal strategy.
history.evolution: The game simplified the complex 'Solo' bidding of German Schafkopf to prioritize the partnership experience, while retaining the '6-is-top' ranking logic.

setup.dealing: Each player receives 9 cards (the entire deck).

rules.objective: Score at least 61 points (out of 120 card points) to win the round.
rules.gameplay: Four players in two partnerships bid 5 to 9 for the right to choose trump. The 6 of the chosen trump suit is highest; then all Kings, Queens, and Jacks in suit order (clubs, spades, hearts, diamonds), then trump suit A-10-9-8-7. Left of dealer leads; must follow suit and must beat the current trick if able. First team to 16 strokes wins.
keyRules: Follow suit; picture cards (J, Q, K) count as trumps.
Must trump if void in led suit; must beat highest card in trick if able.
61+ card points wins the round; 16 strokes win the game.
Tie at 60: redeal same trumps, no bidding. All pass: diamonds, winners score 1 stroke.

strategy.basic: Protect the Kings. In Saskop, Kings are the top tier of the trump suit after the 6. If you have the King of Spades, you have the second most powerful card in the game. Use your high trumps to 'Draw' out the opponents' 10s and Aces early. Don't waste your 6 on a trick that doesn't contain at least 10 points.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Diamond Doubler': If you have a strong hand in Diamonds, bid aggressively. In most Estonian variants, declaring Diamonds as trumps doubles the value of the game points. This is the fastest way to reach the 16-point goal, but also the fastest way to lose points if the opponents capture your 10s.
strategy.advanced: Void Manipulation: Since only 36 cards are in play, suits are short. If you are void in a suit, wait for the opponent to lead it, then 'Slash' it with a medium-rank Jack or Queen. This captures their points without spending your power-cards like the 6 or the Kings. Communication with your partner through 'Throw-away' points is key.
tips: Memorize the 120 total points. If you know you have 55 and your partner just won a trick with a 10, 'Call Out' or stop being defensive.
The 6 is worth zero points but is the ultimate trick-winnerâ€”treat it like a 'Vacuum' for your partner's Aces.

variations.name: Deal method
variations.description: Cutter may specify how cards are dealt: 3 at a time (default), one at a time, 9 at a time, or other patterns such as covers to us, content to us, or face-up until a chosen card appears.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal method is a table convention; no engine constants change.

variations.name: Single picture exchange
variations.description: After the deal, a player with only one picture card (K, Q, or J) may place it face up; partner passes one card face down in exchange.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Optional house rule; engine can support via future exchange phase.

variations.name: Roof signal
variations.description: A player with no picture cards may signal partner (e.g. fingertips forming a roof); some groups allow it, others treat it as illegal.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Signalling is informal; no engine overrides required.

scoring.description: Each round: team with more than 60 of 120 card points wins strokes. First team to 16 strokes wins the game. Card points: K=4, Q=3, J=2, A=11, 10=10; 9-6=0.
scoring.winCondition: First team to reach 16 strokes wins the game. Each round is won by the team that takes more than 60 card points in tricks.
